paragraphs.title: Calling for God's Help and Praying in His Sanctuary

easy.explanation: The psalm begins, "Unto thee will I cry, O LORD my rock."
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist cry?

easy.explanation: The psalmist calls the LORD "my rock."
easy.q: How does the psalmist describe the LORD?

easy.explanation: He asks the LORD to hear "the voice of my supplications."
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to hear?

answers: He fears becoming like those who go down into the pit
He wants to judge his neighbors
He wants to build the sanctuary
medium.explanation: He says that if the LORD is silent, he may become "like them that go down into the pit."
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask the LORD not to be silent?

medium.explanation: He cries unto the LORD while lifting his hands toward God's holy oracle.
medium.q: What physical action accompanies the psalmist's cry?

answers: A holy place of God's presence
medium.explanation: The "holy oracle" refers to the sacred place toward which the psalmist lifts his hands.
medium.q: What does the word "oracle" refer to in this passage?

answers: He depends on the LORD for stability and protection
He wants the LORD to leave him alone
He is praising the strength of the wicked
challenge.explanation: The image of a rock conveys dependability, refuge, and strength.
challenge.q: What does calling the LORD "my rock" suggest about the psalmist's request?

answers: An attempt to hide the prayer
challenge.explanation: The raised hands accompany the psalmist's cry and express earnest prayer.
challenge.q: What does lifting up the hands communicate in this context?

answers: They move from crying to God to describing the act of prayer
They move from praising the wicked to condemning the king
They move from thanksgiving to a call for judgment
challenge.explanation: The psalmist first cries to the LORD and then describes his supplication and raised hands.
challenge.q: How do verses 1–2 develop the psalmist's appeal?

paragraphs.title: Separation from the Wicked and Judgment for Their Deeds

easy.explanation: He asks, "Draw me not away with the wicked."
easy.q: With whom does the psalmist ask not to be drawn away?

easy.explanation: Although they speak peace to their neighbors, "mischief is in their hearts."
easy.q: What is hidden in the hearts of those who speak peace?

easy.explanation: He asks, "Give them according to their deeds."
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to give the wicked?

answers: Their peaceful words conceal evil intentions
They refuse to speak at all
medium.explanation: Their speech sounds peaceful, but mischief is hidden in their hearts.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist not want to be associated with the wicked?

medium.explanation: Their desert is the result or recompense deserved because of their actions.
medium.q: What does "their desert" mean in verse 4?

answers: They do not regard the works of the LORD
They understand all of God's works
medium.explanation: Verse 5 says they do not regard the works of the LORD or the operation of His hands.
medium.q: Why will the LORD destroy the wicked rather than build them up?

answers: Peaceful speech and evil in the heart
challenge.explanation: They speak peace to their neighbors, but mischief is in their hearts.
challenge.q: What central contrast is found in the behavior of the wicked?

answers: People receive recompense corresponding to their deeds
People receive rewards regardless of their actions
Judgment is based only on spoken words
challenge.explanation: The psalm repeats the request that the wicked receive according to their deeds, works, and actions.
challenge.q: How is the principle of judgment expressed in verses 3–4?

answers: The LORD will bring the wicked to ruin rather than establish them
The wicked will refuse to construct a house
The psalmist will not rebuild the sanctuary
challenge.explanation: The phrase contrasts destruction with being established or built up by the LORD.
challenge.q: What does "he shall destroy them, and not build them up" mean?

paragraphs.title: Thanksgiving for Answered Prayer and Trust in God

answers: Because He has heard his supplications
Because He has judged the people
Because He has built a city
easy.explanation: He says, "Blessed be the LORD, because he hath heard the voice of my supplications."
easy.q: Why does the psalmist bless the LORD?

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, "The LORD is my strength and my shield."
easy.q: What does the psalmist call the LORD?

easy.explanation: He says, "therefore my heart greatly rejoiceth."
easy.q: How does the psalmist's heart respond after he is helped?

answers: The LORD heard his supplications and helped him
medium.explanation: The psalmist connects his trust with being heard and helped by the LORD.
medium.q: What led the psalmist to trust in the LORD?

answers: The source of the psalmist's power and courage
A song sung by the wicked
medium.explanation: By calling the LORD his strength, the psalmist identifies Him as his source of power and support.
medium.q: What does "my strength" mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: He says, "with my song will I praise him."
medium.q: How does the psalmist express his praise?

answers: The psalm moves from thanksgiving for answered prayer to confidence and joy
The psalm moves from praise to a request to leave the sanctuary
The psalm moves from describing the wicked to praising their deeds
challenge.explanation: After thanking God for hearing him, the psalmist describes trust, help, rejoicing, and praise.
challenge.q: What change occurs from verse 6 to verse 7?

answers: The psalmist's trust is followed by his testimony that he was helped
Trust prevents the psalmist from praying
Trust belongs only to the wicked
challenge.explanation: He says, "my heart trusted in him, and I am helped."
challenge.q: What is the relationship between trusting the LORD and receiving help?

answers: Peaceful speech, hidden evil, destruction, and rebuilding
challenge.explanation: The psalmist moves from prayer being heard to help, rejoicing, and musical praise.
challenge.q: What emotional sequence appears in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Prayer for the People and the Anointed King

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, "The LORD is their strength."
easy.q: What is the LORD to His people?
For whom does the psalmist ask the LORD to save?

answers: Feed them and lift them up
easy.explanation: He asks the LORD to "feed them also, and lift them up for ever."
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do for His people like a shepherd?

answers: The saving strength of his anointed
medium.explanation: Verse 8 calls the LORD "the saving strength of his anointed."
medium.q: What is the LORD called in relation to His anointed?

answers: The people who belong to the LORD
The dwelling place of the wicked
medium.explanation: The LORD's inheritance refers to His people, who belong to Him.
medium.q: What does "thine inheritance" refer to in this prayer?

answers: Save, bless, feed, and lift up
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks God to save His people, bless His inheritance, feed them, and lift them up forever.
medium.q: Which requests are included in verse 9?

answers: The psalm moves from God's strength for the king and people to prayer for the whole nation
The psalm moves from personal prayer to a description of the wicked
The psalm moves from the sanctuary to thanksgiving for hidden evil
challenge.explanation: The verses first describe God's saving strength and then turn to intercession for His people.
challenge.q: What major movement occurs in verses 8–9?

answers: God should guide, sustain, and protect them
The people should hide evil in their hearts
The people should be judged according to their words alone
challenge.explanation: The shepherd-like language expresses God's care, guidance, support, and protection.
challenge.q: What do the requests to feed and lift up the people suggest?

challenge.explanation: The words "for ever" show that the psalmist asks God to sustain His people continually.
challenge.q: Which phrase emphasizes the lasting nature of the prayer for God's people?
